# NOTES: *The Marriage of Esther* by Guy Boothby (1895, D. Appleton & Co.)

Single book. Metadata: Gutenberg #39731. Title page: "The Marriage of Esther / by Guy Boothby / author of On the Wallaby, etc. / New York, D. Appleton and Company, 1895." Chapters I–XII plus Epilogue. Appended: Appletons' Town and Country Library list (No. 166 = this book) and publisher ads (Doyle, Crockett, Kipling, Hall Caine, Maartens, etc.). Ads are irrelevant to the story.

## CHAPTER I: Two men, a fight, calamitous circumstances
- Setting: bar of Hotel of All Nations, Thursday Island, ~9:35 pm, hot summer evening. Surf audible.
- **Cuthbert Ellison**: tall (over 6 ft), large, muscular; greenish-blue eyes; brown hair and moustache; small flat ears; well-cut features with pronounced nose; wears worn moleskin trousers, patched shirt, cabbage-tree hat, barefoot. Former English gentleman (public school, Oxford), remittance man turned beach-comber. Besetting sin: lying.
- **Silas Murkard**: short, broad-backed, hunchbacked; legs knock at knees; leather patches on trousers; pinched sharp face; craned-forward head; drunk; quotes Apocrypha and Burns. Former gentleman; cynical, sharp-tongued, prophetic-seeming.
- Murkard insults crowd ("spawn"; "How long, my God, how long?"). **Paddy the Lasher** (big pearler) warns him; Murkard quotes Burns ("The honest heart that's free from a' ..."). Paddy punches him above left eyebrow.
- Ellison challenges Paddy outside under Southern Cross. Fight: Ellison breaks Paddy's jaw; Ellison loses use of one eye and a thumb, cut on left ear; mops with barman's handkerchief. Crowd now admires him.
- They camp on hillside east of settlement. Ellison's reflections: once pride; degradation; Jean Paul quote; "besetting sin" of lying. Murkard sleeps; Ellison makes him a pillow of reeds, keeps sentry. Resolves at dawn to reform.
- Dialogue on hill: Murkard jokes ("Serene Mightiness," "Hounds," "Lord Cham—"). Ellison goes to town.
- **Mr. Tugwell** (merchant, store on jetty): offers shilling; Ellison refuses ("I asked you for work, not charity"); returns to apologise; asks half-crown; Tugwell refuses alms.
- **Hong Kong Joe** (boat-builder): refuses due to bruised eye; sends him to **Mah Poo's** store; Mah Poo slams door.
- Ellison walks to jetty, contemplates suicide. Plan: if anyone sets foot on jetty before mail-boat anchors, he lives. A Kanaka boy (~10 yrs) asleep on far side of jetty; anchor drops (bell strikes eight/"twelve o'clock" noted). Ellison lives.
- Back on hill. Murkard: "I was offered a shilling..." Murkard suggests scheme: swim to **Prince of Wales Island**, pearling station of old **McCartney**, whose daughter **Esther** runs it. Ellison disapproves of lying. Murkard: "Since when?" Murkard mentions Ellison's lie the previous night.
- Swim across strait; Murkard nearly drowns (Ellison saves him by hair). Ellison carries him ashore, collapses.

## CHAPTER II: A woman, a recovery, transformations, two resolves
- Ellison finds station: store-shed, Kanakas' hut, kitchen, station house. Curs bark.
- **Esther McCartney**: ~23, handsome, tall, deep brown eyes, nut-brown hair rolled behind head; sun-bonnet; tests Ellison.
- **Mrs. Fenwick**: elderly widow in widow's cap, housekeeper.
- **Jimmy Rhotoma**: big Kanaka, hut-servant/cook helper. Carry Murkard to hut with two camp beds, blue blankets, tin basin, looking-glass.
- Esther: "I don't think you need have told me you were an Englishman." Gives dead Englishman's clothes (man lost six months ago in lugger east of D'Entrecasteaux group). Ellison shaves, dresses.
- Lunch: beef, tomato salad, pickles, cheese, home-brewed beer. Esther reveals she knew the fight story from Paddy the Lasher (one of her hands); shakes his hand.
- Ellison and Murkard talk: Murkard says he told her the truth; Murkard's "Paymaster-General" role. Esther hires Murkard as book-keeper/store-man (£1/week and keep); Ellison as general knockabout hand (same terms).
- Murkard: "I am a creature of two lives." Hints at Esther's secret (a past love). Ellison: "Silas, I don't grasp what you're driving at!" Murkard: "When I saw your face ... on the wharf in Sydney ... the man for whom I was sent into the world... a year of grace."
- Ellison remembers "eight years ago" a night like this, Esther's "guilty secret".
- Ending: Esther says "Good-night!" from veranda; "all the silence of the world seemed to echo that 'Good-night!'"

## CHAPTER III: The world, the flesh, and the devil
- First month: both settled. Murkard loves office work; Esther finds him a mystery; she dislikes him.
- Wood-sawing scene: Esther asks screws; Ellison refuses to say what brought him to Australia; Esther praises his sawing method; Ellison cuts his hand; Esther binds it with her handkerchief. "I should have looked at the saw instead of your face."
- Evening: Ellison meets Esther on beach by alligator-like sandal-wood log; she snubs him ("Good-night!").
- Murkard in boots scene: says Ellison is falling in love; urges him to leave for a month; "Give her a chance... don't drag her down to your hell." Murkard's prayer: "How long, O Lord, how long?" Murkard: "I make my sacrifice for you."
- A week later Esther asks Ellison to row her to Thursday Island. Waits an hour. Mentions Thursday Island; she asks if he's forgiven. Moonlight sail; canvas over her knees.
- Passing the **Hermit's bluff**: grave under tall palm; the Hermit was a tall handsome man with white hair; locket with coronet, photo of great lady, note: "Semper fidelis: Thank God, I can forgive. It is our fate. Good-bye." Others: Bombay Pete, Gray Apollo, Sacramento Dick, the Scholar, John Garfitt (a lord).
- **Ellison's confession**: Eton then Oxford; father the Duke; debts; creditors; a titled lady's false shame story; he took blame and left England; he is **the Marquis of St. Burden**, father the **Duke of Avonturn**. Says "I love you." Esther: "Oh, let me go!" He: "I will go away to-morrow."
- He rows back, cries "Again, again! ... I was tempted and I fell."

## CHAPTER IV: Destiny, an accident, and a betrothal
- Morning: Murkard stony. Ellison says he'll leave. Murkard: "Destiny... my death would be by your hands" dream; "A year... another life between us."
- Ellison proposes to leave; tells Esther goodbye. She faints; he carries her to sofa.
- McCartney returns in luggers; slipped on steps, back injured; paralysed below waist. Ellison breaks news to Esther. McCartney asks Ellison to marry his daughter; Ellison swears; "my whole heart and soul, so help me God!" McCartney gives blessing and dies.
- Doctor (unnamed medico of Thursday Island): "six hours, possibly eight".
- Esther: "Would it make you happier if I stayed?" Yes.
- Ellison fetches doctor. Death: "You have come too late, doctor. He is dead!"

## CHAPTER V: A wedding, a conversation, and an episode
- McCartney buried in cemetery above Port Kennedy (Thursday Island township). Week later wedding in hill-side church; Murkard best man.
- Murkard warns Ellison: Esther's mind "one of the purest"; "watch yourself."
- Veranda talk: Esther asks if he'll regret; he says no. She asks "cleverer and prettier women"; he says "you are my destiny."
- Storm; Murkard seen standing in open with arms raised, then gone. Ellison finds him asleep; Murkard mutters "Be sure your sin will find you out!"

## CHAPTER VI: A temptation, a fall, a series of emotions
- Six months of marriage; pearl shell prices fall; overdraft; bank letter demands halving of overdraft.
- Murkard: "Are you prepared to make a sacrifice for her sake?" Reveals he heard Ellison's confession at Alligator Point while sitting on the rocks. Ellison refuses to ask his father. Murkard: "At whatever cost to myself..." Murkard will go to Government Resident.
- Ellison walks to Hermit's hut site; flees to station. Esther is up: "I shall believe in your honesty and goodness until my life's end."
- Esther pregnant ("the child that is coming").

## CHAPTER VII: Satisfaction, dissatisfaction, and a contemplated arrival
- Murkard goes to Thursday Island; cables duke through Government Resident and banker **Blake**; Murkard guarantees surety.
- Ellison faints at news. Next day: £1,000 credited; more to follow (£4,000 more). Ellison sobs; Murkard says the cable came. Ellison signs papers.
- Ellison gets whiskey; tells Esther; "For your sake I have done..." 
- Mrs. Fenwick reports Esther's labour. Ellison rows off; doctor sends him away for two hours.

## CHAPTER VIII: A vision and a reality
- Ellison sails out at sunset, rows; vision of the dead of the world marching across water in moonlight. Faints. Watch stops at half-past eight.
- Returns; finds Murkard drunk on beach; carries him to hut.
- Doctor: wife and son doing well. Ellison holds son. Sees Esther; gives child back; "God bless and keep you both."

## CHAPTER IX: Happiness, unhappiness, and a man of the world
- Son's birth; Ellison happy. Murkard warns: "Forget it." Ellison resolves to repay £5,000 loan. Plans floating station.
- Ellison leaves for a month with luggers; Esther's farewell ("Go, and may God prosper your labours!").
- 23rd day at sea: Ellison opens oyster, finds enormous **black pearl** (hazel-nut size). Returns home.
- Murkard looks ill (grey, shaking, drunk). Ellison locks pearl in safe (lower drawer); Murkard has a duplicate key.
- **George Merton** (Hon., ~30, handsome, Brankforth Manor, near Exeter, Devon; globe-trotter; "letter of introduction" from Government Resident) arrives. Stays. Sings "Si j'etais Roi!" and Tennyson's "Sweet is true Love."
- Murkard delirium; hut hiding bottles of Hennessey's Cognac in thatch found by Ellison. Ellison confronts/cares.
- Night: Murkard shrieks "I'm falling."; Merton is recognised by Murkard in delirium.

## CHAPTER X: Delirium, a recognition, a departure, and a return
- Murkard's delirium: "You must tell him!"; "Coward!". 
- Merton flirts with Esther; Esther cries to Ellison. "Some day you will hate and despise me..."
- Merton and Murkard meet on beach. Merton: "George Merton of Brankforth Manor". Merton threatens to reveal Murkard's past and Ellison's lie. Demands Murkard leave; Murkard goes.
- Dealer (grey-haired, shrewd) examines pearl; declares it **an imitation**. Ellison thrown.
- Merton helps Ellison: says Murkard is a convicted diamond thief (5 years' penal servitude) and suggests he's the thief.
- Ellison pursues Murkard at night. Murkard confesses: real name **Marquis of St. Burden** (convicted, served sentence, Merton's evidence). Says he cabled the money and that he's the one who helped Ellison. Murkard goes to station.

## CHAPTER XI: Battle and murder
- Merton makes advances to Esther; she strikes him. Merton threatens vengeance. Ellison confronts him: "I intend to kill you."
- Esther clings to Ellison; Merton escapes by boat.
- Ellison takes Winchester rifle; Merton swims back; Murkard follows; Merton stabs Murkard in store; Murkard wounded.
- Ellison arrests Merton with rifle; handcuffs (from nail above desk); guards in hut.
- Murkard, dying, reveals pearl hidden in matchbox behind box in store corner; pearl recovered. Murkard: "Tell them I died doing my duty." Says Merton: "five years is a long time to wait."
- Murkard dies ("Silas Murkard's soul's account had gone to be audited by the Auditor of Heaven").

## CHAPTER XII: Conclusion and epilogue
- Esther, Ellison reconcile. Ellison tells her everything except the murder. Esther: "Murkard... thief and murderer."
- Police: Merton drowned, jumped from boat while handcuffed crossing strait.
- Ellison resolves never to yield to temptation again.

## EPILOGUE
- ~18 months later, Tahiti (Papeete); narrator meets Ellison and wife, and their schooner. Son named **Murkard**. Ellison sold station.
- Narrator writes book with promises: do wife and Murkard justice; "let me down as lightly as possible."
- Levuka, Fiji: title *The Marriage of Esther*.
